description: Register of the e-commerce hardening audit findings (severity P0, P1 and P2). The release gates NO_OPEN_P0 and NO_OPEN_P1 read this file: scripts/release/ecommerce-release-gates.mjs.
seeded_from: ecommerce hardening audit of 2026-10-01: twelve domain readers plus independent verification of the P1 and top P2 findings (PG17 with the 158-migration baseline)

rules.open: Blocks PRODUCTION_READY when the severity is P0 or P1.
rules.fixed: Needs fixed_by: the commit or the migration that fixes it. Without it a P0/P1 still blocks.
rules.accepted_risk: Needs a non-empty notes field saying who accepted the risk and why. Without it a P0/P1 still blocks.
rules.external_gate: Depends on a third party or on the owner. Needs a non-empty notes field saying what it waits on and from whom; without it a P0/P1 still blocks. With notes it does not block PRODUCTION_READY and is reported separately as a blocker of the public launch.
rules.severity: The reader severity is kept, and for a cluster of aliases the worst one. verification[].severity is what the independent verifier graded; changing severity is a decision for the lead and belongs in notes.
rules.aliases: The same defect reported by another reader. An alias is closed together with its canonical finding.

findings.title: Panel stock edit overwrites products.stock with the counted number: reserved units ignored, no concurrency check, no ledger row; this oversells
findings.notes: The count sent by the sheet, the plan and the product form is translated like the Caja Clara count (available = max(count - reserved, 0), ledger row, stock conflict when the count does not cover the reserved units), with an optional expected_stock guard (PT409). The Panel scanner count sends only a difference against the available figure and cannot be translated: while the product has reserved units it is refused (22023, STOCK_COUNT_HAS_RESERVED) and points to the catalog count. Client follow-ups, not blocking: the Panel still prefills the count field with the available figure (errs on the safe side) and does not send expected_stock; stage_catalog_products (import_catalog_batch) still writes an absolute stock.

findings.title: A non-2xx on the merchant-order lookup turns a legitimate approved payment into a permanent security review with no recovery or refund path
findings.fixed_by: 5d0c366 (the failed read no longer records an empty preference) · 12f79b8 · 18dcb08 (a charge in review can be recovered into an order or refunded)
findings.notes: Closed in two halves. Database (18dcb08): an approved payment parked in security review without an order can be recovered into an order or refunded. Edge (5d0c366): a failed merchant-order read raises instead of recording an empty preference, so the false preference_mismatch is no longer produced. Residuals, by decision: a payment that has neither an order id nor a preference id is still recorded with an empty preference and goes to manual review (now with a recovery and a refund path); a permanent merchant-order failure (404) retries to dead_letter, which raises the CRITICAL queue alert, instead of going to manual review. Provider simulated: not exercised against real Mercado Pago.
findings.where: supabase/functions/_shared/mercadopago.ts fetchMerchantOrder (L318-322) and paymentSnapshot (L343-347); public.record_mercadopago_payment_snapshot; callers mercadopago-payment-worker/index.ts L101-108 and mercadopago-checkout-status/index.ts L92-97

findings.title: Production has no steady-state switch for real payments: every production preference needs the 'smoke' secret that runbooks and tooling require to be absent, and the failure happens after stock is reserved
findings.fixed_by: 4b3f40f (gate before any reservation) · 6e7af1d4 (Edge switch) · 297130a7 (REAL_MONEY_GATE) · cb7f60f2 (config checker) · d4e5fa13 (runbooks)
findings.notes: FIXED in the branch, NOT deployed (owner decision 2026-10-02, option A: an explicit, permanent backend switch). In production a charge is created only when all three keys hold: project review approved (MERCADOPAGO_PRODUCTION_REVIEW_STATUS=approved), the business has Mercado Pago enabled in production with its connected production seller, and the Edge secret MERCADOPAGO_REAL_MONEY_ENABLED holds exactly 'enabled' (anything else is closed; compared raw). One pure definition (real-money-gate.ts) is evaluated by assertPaymentCreationGate (checkout session before any reservation; preference), by mercadopago-create-preference before prepare_mercadopago_preference_v2 (closes a fail-open: new_attempt re-reserved stock before the gate), and by createPreference right before the only POST that creates a charge. Closed: 409 PAYMENTS_NOT_ENABLED, no reservation, no provider call. The legacy MERCADOPAGO_REAL_PAYMENT_SMOKE_CONFIRMATION opens nothing; the config checker reports it and sincronizar-worker-hmac.mjs refuses to run with it. Test environment: switch not required; real money excluded by the credential itself. Money going back never consults the switch (refund, cancel, webhook, worker, reconciliation, status: Deno tests with the switch off). REAL_MONEY_GATE prints MONEY_MOVEMENT_POSSIBLE (YES/NO/UNKNOWN; UNKNOWN never passes) from the secrets' SHA-256 digests (the Management API returns value = sha256(secret), verified on Staging). CP today: review present, no legacy variable, no switch: stays closed. Deploy the new functions BEFORE ever setting the switch. Residuals: a preference already handed to a buyer stays payable until its checkout expires; the storefront availability does not see the switch (the checkout then refuses with no reservation). Implemented by an agent in an isolated worktree, reviewed by the lead (runtime predicates equivalent to the previous ones, fail-closed paths), suites green: Deno 52+452, test:payments 228, release gates 150.

findings.title: production-health-check.mjs can never be green and can never see a CRITICAL alert

It also required exactly four taba-* jobs (migrations schedule nine; CP has five) and only accepted the old production ref, so it could never be green and refused to look at CONTROLLED_PRODUCTION. findings.notes: Found by the staging certification runner: refusals with SQLSTATE 55000 came back as HTTP 500 (PostgREST maps the whole class 55 to 500, and the P0 family except P0001 as well, so a "not found" P0002 was also a 500: defect C-2 of the certifier). Closed on the server side (owner decision). 20261002090000 wraps the current body of 109 API entry functions in a boundary handler that, only when the call comes through the API (request.method set) and only in the outermost PL/pgSQL frame, re-raises 55000 as HTTP 409 and P0002 as HTTP 404 with the same body (code, message, details, hint); calls without request.method and nested PL/pgSQL callers still see the original SQLSTATE. 20261002091000 gives 46 client refusals in 5 functions the SQLSTATE of what they mean instead of P0001. Policy: docs/ecommerce-hardening/http-contract.md. Regression: supabase/tests/http_error_contract_test.sql (42), tests/http-error-contract.test.mjs, and the certifier through a real PostgREST (pricing:API_01_BUSINESS_REFUSAL_55000_ANSWERS_HTTP_409, cancellation:ORDER_NOT_FOUND_IS_ANSWERED_AS_A_CLIENT_ERROR, REFUSAL_STATUS 55000->409, P0002->404). The Panel (classifyRpcError and the two outbox result builders in js/production-operations.js) already treats a 409 as final, so js/ did not change. Still answering 500, by ownership: the 40 entries of POS/Caja, fiscal, the print agent and the six legacy payment functions, and the two SQL entries mp_consume_oauth / mp_claim_refresh. Rollback order: 20261002091000 first, then 20261002090000 (the 090000 rollback refuses while 091000 is applied). Both migrations refuse to apply (ROLLOUT_BLOCKED) when a wrapped function body differs from the one they were generated from.

findings.title: An unverified checkout closes by time: past the 48-hour probe window CHECKOUT_PROVIDER_UNVERIFIED is auto-resolved as 'condition absent' and the truth sweep stops, with no proof that the buyer did not pay
findings.notes: Reproduced on the branch (208 migrations, local database built with the gate's image and sequence): a checkout that reached Mercado Pago, expired and only had non-conclusive empties (seller connection changed) or no answered probe had its alert open at 47 h and resolved by the system at 49 h ('Condición ausente en la reconciliación automática.'), and enqueue_checkout_provider_probes stopped asking. Same silent ending PAY-PROBE-01 fixed for empties, 48 hours later. Fix: past the window the alert closes only on proof (a conclusive empty, the provider payment, the order) or on an active owner/admin resolution with a note (same rule as PAYMENT_NEEDS_REVIEW; a staff resolution is reopened); the sweep keeps one probe per day up to 30 days for those checkouts; a per-environment watermark (now - 48 h at apply time) keeps older history out of the alerts (scripts/payments/reconcile-payments.mjs still covers it; without the row everything is watched). Test: unverified_checkout_never_closes_by_time_test.sql (45; fails without the migration). Rollback drill: schema fingerprint identical before/after rollback, rollback and forward both re-runnable.
